questions.q: How does Unity Catalog build its lineage graph?
options: Automatically, by observing every Spark query that runs against Unity Catalog tables — nobody writes or maintains a lineage diagram by hand
A data engineer must manually draw and update a lineage diagram
It requires a separate, dedicated lineage-tracking cluster
Lineage only appears if explicitly requested via a special SQL command before each query
questions.explain: Databricks builds it by observing every query Chapter 3's actual pipeline already ran.

questions.q: What's the difference between table-level and column-level lineage?
options: Table-level shows which tables feed a table; column-level traces which specific upstream columns fed a specific downstream column
They show exactly the same information, just formatted differently
Column-level lineage only works on managed tables, not external ones
Table-level lineage is manual while column-level is automatic
questions.explain: Column-level answers a narrower, often more useful question about one specific value's origin.

questions.q: How does lineage help before making a risky schema change, like dropping a column?
options: It shows every downstream table that depends on that column, letting you check for breakage before making the change rather than after
It automatically prevents any schema change from being made
It has no relationship to schema changes at all
It only shows lineage after the change has already been made
questions.explain: This turns "what else reads this?" from a guess into something you can check directly beforehand.

questions.q: Why wouldn't a table populated entirely outside Databricks show up in the lineage graph?
options: Lineage capture depends on operations running through Spark against Unity Catalog-governed tables — bypassing Spark means no lineage is captured
External tools are always automatically tracked, just with a delay
Lineage only fails to capture data written using SQL, not PySpark
Every table shows up in lineage regardless of how it was populated
questions.explain: This is a real, concrete payoff of building the pipeline the way this course actually built it — through Spark.

questions.q: In this course's pipeline, what does column-level lineage trace for gold.daily_revenue's total_revenue column?
options: Back through silver.trips.fare_amount and further back through bronze.trips.fare_amount, the exact column at every hop
Only the table name, with no column-level detail at all
Every column in every table in the nyc_taxi catalog, without distinction
Nothing, since total_revenue is a computed aggregate with no traceable origin
questions.explain: This traces through Lesson 28's sum("fare_amount") and Lesson 27's .cast("double") specifically.
